title: codemother finds her held questions through the librarian's trees tool
intention: The trees tool gains CROSS_DOMAIN_QUESTIONS, the keyed tree the librarian plants the corpus in, and the corpus module's TABLE becomes it.
why: 2026-11-12: build_inspector encapsulation_holds rows cairn/devices/codemother/seed_trees.py:50 and cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_codemother_holds_the_librarians_questions.py:47 -> cairn/devices/librarian; the corpus tree librarian_cross_domain_questions is planted live with 32 keys, and trees.find('Q-cog-001') returns its text, meta {origin, function} and provenance said_by.
traces_to: RULE 1 and outline 2.3.7 (a device reaches another only over the bus or a tool it publishes) and 4.4.2 (a delegate working its trees through the trees tool is not a breach).
how: The trees tool gains CROSS_DOMAIN_QUESTIONS, the keyed tree the librarian plants the corpus in, and the corpus module's TABLE becomes it. seed_trees._sections finds each held id by key with trees.find(qid, table=...) and takes text, function, origin and said_by from the newest leaf; seed() takes table= (the corpus tree when absent). The d12f proof reads the corpus off the tree through store.read and trees.find. New proof cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_codemother_finds_held_questions_through_the_trees_tool.py.

clauses.claim: no file under cairn/devices/codemother imports librarian code but its published tools
seed(dry_run=True, table=<scratch keyed leaf>) takes each held entry's text, function, origin and said_by from the leaf found by its id, and an id the leaf does not carry is reported in errors
the trees tool names the corpus tree as CROSS_DOMAIN_QUESTIONS, and every id cognition_questions.json holds is found there on the live store

decisions.text: D1: trees.py gains CROSS_DOMAIN_QUESTIONS beside OWNER; cross_domain_questions.TABLE imports it.
D2: seed_trees._sections(data, errors, table) resolves held ids with trees.find; seed() takes table=, defaulting to trees.CROSS_DOMAIN_QUESTIONS.
D3: the d12f proof's _corpus reads the tree (store.read keys, trees.find each); its tooth 5 asserts trees.find and no corpus-module import. A new proof carries this ticket's three teeth.

out: the corpus JSON and its load/plant
